properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean formation comprises Lower Carboniferous (Tournaisian–Viséan) sedimentary strata of the Strathclyde Group, dominated by interbedded siltstones, sandstones, and volcanic basaltic intrusions characteristic of the Lothian basin. Principal structural masonry is pale blonde-to-grey quartz-arenite Craigleith sandstone, supplemented by carbonaceous Hailes sandstone, bonded with non-hydraulic to weakly hydraulic slaked lime mortar and fine river sand aggregates. Subsurface hydrology slopes northwestward toward the Water of Leith incised gorge, governed by historical French drainage channels beneath cobbled area wells and cellar vaults.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis:
Ainslie Place Gardens contains mature broadleaf urban canopy specimens:
- *Acer pseudoplatanus* (Sycamore) and *Ulmus glabra* (Wych Elm), exhibiting massive multi-stem crown spreads with fully developed late-summer deep green foliage, dense branch matrices, and minor leaf-tier chlorosis.
- *Tilia × europaea* (Common Lime) and *Betula pendula* (Silver Birch), displaying upright form, dense leaf distribution, and defined radial root flares anchoring within maintained perennial turf and curved gravel pedestrian circuits.

properties.architectural_summary: Neoclassical Greek Revival / Regency urban palace-fronted crescent terraces designed by architect James Gillespie Graham (1822–1828) for the Moray Estate. Uniform four-storey elevation profile comprising sunken basement service areas with flagstone bridging, rusticated ashlar ground storeys, two polished ashlar principal storeys, and low-profile slate mansard attic storeys behind stone blocking courses. Facades articulate strict tripartite vertical bay rhythms, channelled ashlar rustication on base courses, molded platbands, classical stringcourses, and dentiled eaves cornices. Symmetrical multi-flue rectangular ashlar chimney stacks with terracotta cylindrical pots crest slate roof ridges. Fenestration is rectified to rigid plumb lines, featuring regular 6-over-6 and 2-over-2 double-hung timber sash-and-case windows set into molded architraves.
